checkedAlternates.risk: A phone call is spoken in real time, which feels as direct as talking to someone in the room.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The fourth row needs the other person in sight; a call only works because a network carries the voice, which the text and the email anchor.

checkedAlternates.risk: A whistle is how people call a dog or a horse, so it can read as sending a message through an animal.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The whistle reaches a person within earshot; the pigeon is the only item where the animal carries the message somewhere else.

checkedAlternates.risk: Digital postcards are sent by email, and holiday apps use the word freely.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The item is the printed card that needs a stamp, grouped with the letter for exactly that reason.

checkedAlternates.risk: Shouting into a phone is common enough to blur the row.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A shout on its own carries only as far as your voice, which is the face-to-face rule.

authorReview.notes: The four rows are four carriers: an animal, the post, a network, and nothing at all. The phone call is the only item where the carrier is invisible.

blindPlaytest.notes: The phone call is the sharpest edge. If testers put it face to face, replace it with a fax and note that the row is about the network, not the delay.
